The area of the region {(x,y):∣x∣+∣y∣≤1}\{(x, y) : |x| + |y| \le 1\}{(x,y):∣x∣+∣y∣≤1} is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Area under a line y=f(x)y = f(x)y=f(x) from x=ax = ax=a to x=bx = bx=b is ∫aby dx\displaystyle\int_a^b y\,dx∫ab​ydx.

  1. 1

    In the first quadrant the boundary is the line x+y=1x + y = 1x+y=1

    y=1−x,0≤x≤1y = 1 - x,\quad 0 \le x \le 1y=1−x,0≤x≤1
  2. 2

    The region is symmetric about both axes: four equal parts

    A=4∫01(1−x) dxA = 4\displaystyle\int_0^1 (1 - x)\,dxA=4∫01​(1−x)dx
  3. 3

    Integrate and put the limits; so the option is (D)

    A=4[x−x22]01=4×12=2A = 4\left[x - \dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^1 = 4 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 2A=4[x−2x2​]01​=4×21​=2A=4[x−x22]01=4×12=2\displaystyle A = 4\left[x - \dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^1 = 4 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 2A=4[x−2x2​]01​=4×21​=2
    1
Answer(D) 2\displaystyle 22 sq units

Watch out Stopping at the first-quadrant part, 12\dfrac{1}{2}21​, option (C); the region has four equal parts.

Formula / idea Area between a curve and the y-axis: ∫cdx dy\displaystyle\int_c^d x\,dy∫cd​xdy

  1. 1

    For −1≤y≤1-1 \le y \le 1−1≤y≤1, x=2y+3>0x = 2y + 3 > 0x=2y+3>0: the region lies right of the y-axis

    A=∫−11(2y+3) dyA = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} (2y + 3)\,dyA=∫−11​(2y+3)dyA=∫−11(2y+3) dy\displaystyle A = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} (2y + 3)\,dyA=∫−11​(2y+3)dy
  2. 2

    Integrate and put the limits; so the option is (C)

    A=[y2+3y]−11=(1+3)−(1−3)=6A = \left[y^2 + 3y\right]_{-1}^{1} = (1 + 3) - (1 - 3) = 6A=[y2+3y]−11​=(1+3)−(1−3)=6A=[y2+3y]−11=(1+3)−(1−3)=6\displaystyle A = \left[y^2 + 3y\right]_{-1}^{1} = (1 + 3) - (1 - 3) = 6A=[y2+3y]−11​=(1+3)−(1−3)=6

Question 4Question 6

Question 6 of 20, Level 1

6Assertion-ReasonBoard-pattern1 mark
Assertion (A): The area of the region bounded by the curve y=xy = \sqrt{x}y=x​, the x-axis and the line x=4x = 4x=4 is 163\dfrac{16}{3}316​ sq units. Reason (R): The area of the region bounded by the curve y=xy = \sqrt{x}y=x​, the y-axis and the line y=2y = 2y=2 is also 163\dfrac{16}{3}316​ sq units.

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Area with the x-axis is ∫y dx\displaystyle\int y\,dx∫ydx; area with the y-axis is ∫x dy\displaystyle\int x\,dy∫xdy.

  1. 1

    For A: vertical strips from x=0x = 0x=0 to x=4x = 4x=4

    ∫04x dx=23[x3/2]04=163\displaystyle\int_0^4 \sqrt{x}\,dx = \dfrac{2}{3}\left[x^{3/2}\right]_0^4 = \dfrac{16}{3}∫04​x​dx=32​[x3/2]04​=316​∫04x dx=23[x3/2]04=163\displaystyle \displaystyle\int_0^4 \sqrt{x}\,dx = \dfrac{2}{3}\left[x^{3/2}\right]_0^4 = \dfrac{16}{3}∫04​x​dx=32​[x3/2]04​=316​
  2. 2

    So A is true

  3. 3

    For R: x=y2x = y^2x=y2; horizontal strips from y=0y = 0y=0 to y=2y = 2y=2

    ∫02y2 dy=[y33]02=83\displaystyle\int_0^2 y^2\,dy = \left[\dfrac{y^3}{3}\right]_0^2 = \dfrac{8}{3}∫02​y2dy=[3y3​]02​=38​∫02y2 dy=[y33]02=83\displaystyle \displaystyle\int_0^2 y^2\,dy = \left[\dfrac{y^3}{3}\right]_0^2 = \dfrac{8}{3}∫02​y2dy=[3y3​]02​=38​

    Check: 163+83=8\dfrac{16}{3} + \dfrac{8}{3} = 8316​+38​=8, the 4×24 \times 24×2 rectangle.

  4. 4

    The area is 83\dfrac{8}{3}38​, not 163\dfrac{16}{3}316​, so R is false

  5. 5

    A is true and R is false, so the option is (C)

    1
Answer(C) A is true, but R is false

Watch out Assuming both regions are equal; together they fill the 4×24 \times 24×2 rectangle, so they are 163\dfrac{16}{3}316​ and 83\dfrac{8}{3}38​.

    Area of the part from x=0x = 0x=0 to x=kx = kx=k

    A1=2∫0kx dx=43k3/2A_1 = 2\displaystyle\int_0^k \sqrt{x}\,dx = \dfrac{4}{3}k^{3/2}A1​=2∫0k​x​dx=34​k3/2A1=2∫0kx dx=43k3/2\displaystyle A_1 = 2\displaystyle\int_0^k \sqrt{x}\,dx = \dfrac{4}{3}k^{3/2}A1​=2∫0k​x​dx=34​k3/2

    Put A1=12AA_1 = \dfrac{1}{2}AA1​=21​A

    43k3/2=163⇒k3/2=4\dfrac{4}{3}k^{3/2} = \dfrac{16}{3} \Rightarrow k^{3/2} = 434​k3/2=316​⇒k3/2=443k3/2=163⇒k3/2=4\displaystyle \dfrac{4}{3}k^{3/2} = \dfrac{16}{3} \Rightarrow k^{3/2} = 434​k3/2=316​⇒k3/2=4

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

  1. 1

    Eliminate ttt: put t=y2at = \dfrac{y}{2a}t=2ay​ in x=at2x = at^2x=at2

    x=a⋅y24a2⇒y2=4axx = a \cdot \dfrac{y^2}{4a^2} \Rightarrow y^2 = 4axx=a⋅4a2y2​⇒y2=4axx=a⋅y24a2⇒y2=4ax\displaystyle x = a \cdot \dfrac{y^2}{4a^2} \Rightarrow y^2 = 4axx=a⋅4a2y2​⇒y2=4ax
    ½
  2. 2

    The ordinates: t=1t = 1t=1 gives x=ax = ax=a; t=2t = 2t=2 gives x=4ax = 4ax=4a

    ½
  3. 3

    The region is symmetric about the x-axis; upper half y=2axy = 2\sqrt{ax}y=2ax​

    A=2∫a4a2a x dxA = 2\displaystyle\int_a^{4a} 2\sqrt{a}\,\sqrt{x}\,dxA=2∫a4a​2a​x​dxA=2∫a4a2a x dx\displaystyle A = 2\displaystyle\int_a^{4a} 2\sqrt{a}\,\sqrt{x}\,dxA=2∫a4a​2a​x​dx
    1
  4. 4

    Integrate

    A=4a⋅23[x3/2]a4a=8a3(8a3/2−a3/2)A = 4\sqrt{a} \cdot \dfrac{2}{3}\left[x^{3/2}\right]_a^{4a} = \dfrac{8\sqrt{a}}{3}\left(8a^{3/2} - a^{3/2}\right)A=4a​⋅32​[x3/2]a4a​=38a​​(8a3/2−a3/2)A=4a⋅23[x3/2]a4a=8a3(8a3/2−a3/2)\displaystyle A = 4\sqrt{a} \cdot \dfrac{2}{3}\left[x^{3/2}\right]_a^{4a} = \dfrac{8\sqrt{a}}{3}\left(8a^{3/2} - a^{3/2}\right)A=4a​⋅32​[x3/2]a4a​=38a​​(8a3/2−a3/2)
    ½
  5. 5

    Required area

    A=8a3⋅7a3/2=56a23 sq unitsA = \dfrac{8\sqrt{a}}{3} \cdot 7a^{3/2} = \dfrac{56a^2}{3}\ \text{sq units}A=38a​​⋅7a3/2=356a2​ sq unitsA=8a3⋅7a3/2=56a23 sq units\displaystyle A = \dfrac{8\sqrt{a}}{3} \cdot 7a^{3/2} = \dfrac{56a^2}{3}\ \text{sq units}A=38a​​⋅7a3/2=356a2​ sq units
    ½
Answer56a23\displaystyle \dfrac{56a^2}{3}356a2​ sq units

    ∫−42∣x+1∣ dx=∫−4−1−(x+1) dx+∫−12(x+1) dx\displaystyle\int_{-4}^{2} |x + 1|\,dx = \displaystyle\int_{-4}^{-1} -(x + 1)\,dx + \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} (x + 1)\,dx∫−42​∣x+1∣dx=∫−4−1​−(x+1)dx+∫−12​(x+1)dx∫−42∣x+1∣ dx=∫−4−1−(x+1) dx+∫−12(x+1) dx\displaystyle \displaystyle\int_{-4}^{2} |x + 1|\,dx = \displaystyle\int_{-4}^{-1} -(x + 1)\,dx + \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} (x + 1)\,dx∫−42​∣x+1∣dx=∫−4−1​−(x+1)dx+∫−12​(x+1)dx

  3. 3

    Integrate

    =−[(x+1)22]−4−1+[(x+1)22]−12= -\left[\dfrac{(x + 1)^2}{2}\right]_{-4}^{-1} + \left[\dfrac{(x + 1)^2}{2}\right]_{-1}^{2}=−[2(x+1)2​]−4−1​+[2(x+1)2​]−12​=−[(x+1)22]−4−1+[(x+1)22]−12\displaystyle = -\left[\dfrac{(x + 1)^2}{2}\right]_{-4}^{-1} + \left[\dfrac{(x + 1)^2}{2}\right]_{-1}^{2}=−[2(x+1)2​]−4−1​+[2(x+1)2​]−12​
    ½

    Put the limits

    =−(0−92)+(92−0)=9= -\left(0 - \dfrac{9}{2}\right) + \left(\dfrac{9}{2} - 0\right) = 9=−(0−29​)+(29​−0)=9=−(0−92)+(92−0)=9\displaystyle = -\left(0 - \dfrac{9}{2}\right) + \left(\dfrac{9}{2} - 0\right) = 9=−(0−29​)+(29​−0)=9

    It represents the area bounded by y=∣x+1∣y = |x + 1|y=∣x+1∣, the x-axis and the lines x=−4x = -4x=−4, x=2x = 2x=2

Case Study: A housing society has an elliptical lawn whose boundary is the ellipse x2100+y264=1\dfrac{x^2}{100} + \dfrac{y^2}{64} = 1100x2​+64y2​=1, with its centre at the origin (units in metres). At the centre there is a circular fountain pool with boundary x2+y2=16x^2 + y^2 = 16x2+y2=16. Grass covers the lawn everywhere outside the pool. A straight footpath of negligible width joins the points (10,0)(10, 0)(10,0) and (0,8)(0, 8)(0,8) on the boundary. Based on this information, answer the following questions using integration.
  1. (i)Find the area enclosed by the fountain pool.1 mark
  2. (ii)Find the area enclosed by the elliptical boundary of the lawn.1 mark
  3. (iii)(a)Find the area of the part of the lawn in the first quadrant that lies between the footpath and the boundary.2 marks
  4. OR
  5. (iii)(b)Find the area of the grassed part of the lawn lying in the first quadrant.2 marks

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea ∫a2−x2 dx=x2a2−x2+a22sin⁡−1xa+C\displaystyle\int \sqrt{a^2 - x^2}\,dx = \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^2 - x^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a} + C∫a2−x2​dx=2x​a2−x2​+2a2​sin−1ax​+C

(i)1 mark

  1. 1

    Pool radius =4= 4=4; the circle is symmetric about both axes

    A=4∫0416−x2 dx=4[x216−x2+8sin⁡−1x4]04A = 4\displaystyle\int_0^4 \sqrt{16 - x^2}\,dx = 4\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{16 - x^2} + 8\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{4}\right]_0^4A=4∫04​16−x2​dx=4[2x​16−x2​+8sin−14x​]04​A=4∫0416−x2 dx=4[x216−x2+8sin⁡−1x4]04\displaystyle A = 4\displaystyle\int_0^4 \sqrt{16 - x^2}\,dx = 4\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{16 - x^2} + 8\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{4}\right]_0^4A=4∫04​16−x2​dx=4[2x​16−x2​+8sin−14x​]04​
    ½
  2. 2

    Put the limits

    A=4×8⋅π2=16π m2A = 4 \times 8 \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{2} = 16\pi\ \text{m}^2A=4×8⋅2π​=16π m2A=4×8⋅π2=16π m2\displaystyle A = 4 \times 8 \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{2} = 16\pi\ \text{m}^2A=4×8⋅2π​=16π m2
    ½
Answer (i)16π m2\displaystyle 16\pi\ \text{m}^216π m2

(ii)1 mark

    Put the limits

(iii)(a)2 marks
